title: When Breath Becomes Air
author: Paul Kalanithi
target_audience: General readers interested in personal memoirs
Individuals coping with illness, mortality, or grief
core_themes: Mortality and the meaning of life
Identity and purpose in the face of death
The philosophy of living and dying
The pursuit of knowledge and excellence
primary_purpose: To share the profound journey of a young neurosurgeon facing terminal cancer, exploring what makes life meaningful in the face of death, and to bridge the worlds of science, medicine, and literature through personal reflection.

structure_format.organization: Divided into two main parts: 'In Perfect Health I Begin' (Kalanithi's early life and medical career) and 'Cease Not till Death' (his illness and facing mortality), followed by an epilogue by his wife.
features: Philosophical inquiries about life and death
Descriptions of medical cases and experiences
A concluding epilogue offering closure from the family perspective

key_concepts_lessons: Confronting mortality brings clarity to what truly matters in life.
Medicine is about forging human connections as much as clinical skill.
Identity can be challenged and redefined by illness.
Purpose and meaning are constructed even in the most difficult circumstances.
It is possible to find grace and dignity in the face of suffering and death.
Living each day fully is an imperative when time is limited.
notable_features: Written during the author’s battle with terminal lung cancer
Bridges the physician's and patient's perspective on illness
Includes insights from literature, philosophy, and neuroscience
Final epilogue written by Paul Kalanithi’s wife, Lucy
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2016 in the US, ‘When Breath Becomes Air’ emerged at a time of heightened discussion about end-of-life care, physician well-being, and patient perspectives in modern medicine. The book resonated particularly in a culture interested in living meaningfully in the face of uncertainty.
reception_impact: New York Times bestseller and highly acclaimed globally
Praised for its literary merit, emotional depth, and honesty
Frequently recommended by healthcare professionals, book clubs, and academic programs
Inspired conversations about mortality, meaning, and the human side of medicine
comparable_titles: The Bright Hour by Nina Riggs
The Emperor of All Maladies by Siddhartha Mukherjee
Tuesdays with Morrie by Mitch Albom
The Last Lecture by Randy Pausch
